On a cluster whose home directory is on NFS, xcrunner now runs containers with the faster ns engine by itself, and inputs reached through a symlinked folder are mounted.

## A node-local container folder, chosen automatically

An overlay layer cannot live on NFS, so with the runtime home on a shared filesystem every container fell back to PRoot. When neither `XCRUNNER_CONTAINER_DIR` nor `XCRUNNER_ENV_LAYER_DIR` is set and the default container folder fails the overlay probe, xcrunner now uses a private `xcrunner-<user>` folder under `/tmp` (then `$TMPDIR`) that passes it and has 10 GB free.

- The choice is made each time a runtime starts, on the node where containers run, and cached per boot. A folder set at project init on a login node would be the wrong disk on a compute node.
- The image store stays where it is. Explicit settings always win; `XCRUNNER_AUTO_LOCAL_DIRS=0` turns the choice off.
- `xcrunner info` shows it as `containers_auto` and `env_layer_dir`.
- Installed packages in the env layer now live per node: a new node installs them once.

## Bind mounts through a symlinked folder

A bind source whose path ran through an absolute symlink (`inputs/data -> /shared/dataset`) resolved inside the container after `pivot_root`, looked missing, and was skipped without a word. cwltool stages files that way, and Cell Ranger ARC reported "No input FASTQs were found". Bind sources are now resolved on the host when the container is created, as Docker does.

## Other changes

- A `--mount` whose source does not exist is refused with Docker's message, instead of leaving an empty mountpoint.
- The coala adapter describes each container (xcrunner version, engine, container folder), for coala-runtime's execution log.
